item.title: Memory & Aging: What's Normal, What's Not, and What You Can Do About It — Thu Jul 30, 2:00 PM — Toronto Reference Library
item.description: Psychologist Nicole Anderson discusses how different kinds of cognitive functions change as a part of healthy aging and provides examples of normal memory slips and not-so-normal memory slips. This presentation discusses factors affecting cognition, including medical factors and everyday lifestyle factors, then provides a number of memory strategies that people can use to improve their memory function. Nicole Anderson is the Senior Scientist at the Rotman Research Institute (Baycrest) and Professor, Psychology and Psychiatry (University of Toronto). She is the author of "Living with mild cognitive impairment: a guide to maximizing brain health and reducing risk of dementia" Information Collection Notice: The personal information on this form is collected by the Toronto Public Library under the Public Libraries Act, sections 20(a), 20(c), and 20(d). item.title: Branch Art Exhibit: Mickey Arts Exhibition — Sat Aug 1, 12:00 AM — Deer Park
item.description: Throughout the month of August, the works of artist Michael Alemayehu are on display at Deer Park branch . Michael Alemayehu is a self-taught Ethiopian artist based in Canada. Through graphite and colored pencils, he creates realistic portraits and wildlife art. His work reflects his heritage and passion for detail, inviting viewers to see the beauty of Africa and beyond. "Art has always been my language of expression and connection. Inspired by my Ethiopian roots, I use realism to honor culture, identity, and nature. With every drawing, I aim to spark fascination and share stories that celebrate beauty and tradition." This exhibit is part of TPL's Art Exhibit Space program. Toronto Public Library provides space for local artists to exhibit their work at locations across the city. These exhibits aim to reflect the diverse cultural interests of the city and its neighbourhoods. The exhibit can be viewed during Deer Park's open hours. item.title: Lost in the Labyrinth — Tue Aug 4, 5:00 PM — Trinity Square Labyrinth
item.description:
Address: Trinity Square Labyrinth Behind the Eaton Centre, easy access off of Bay Street! Toronto, ON Canada
Come downtown and walk through two labyrinths, one intentional at Trinity Square and one accidentally created inside the now empty Hudson’s Bay building. Both which I will be guiding us through in their entirety. One of my favorite things about Toronto are its endless back alleys and secret spots that you stumble onto when wandering around. Most recently that was the Trinity Labyrinth, a wonderful installation tucked away behind the Eaton Centre. While it's strange to feel bad for a public art installation it's rare to find one that's so explicitly begging for pedestrians to engage with…
Hosted by Craig Meerkamper & Adam Chen

item.description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto This session explains how secure access is built and managed in OneLake. It covers an overview of OneLake security, the data access control model, creating and managing roles, SQL analytics endpoint security, and granular controls for tables, folders, columns, and rows. The goal is to give attendees a clear understanding of how these settings fit together so they can configure access more confidently and avoid common issues when securing data in Fabric.
Source: Meetup: Microsoft Reactor Toronto

item.title: Step In, Stand Out: Navigating Your First 90 Days at Work — Wed Aug 5, 12:00 PM
item.description:
The first 90 days in a new job set the tone for your long-term success and this workshop will equip you to step in with clarity and stand out with confidence. Together, we will walk through a structured roadmap built around five key phases: learning and observation, relationship-building, performance and communication excellence, personal brand and visibility, and finally, a powerful bonus 10-day introspection period to help you evaluate alignment and ensure the role truly fits you. You will learn how to adapt to workplace culture, build authentic relationships, ask smart questions, and demonstrate value early. By the end, you will leave with a practical 100-day success plan designed to help you build the next steps of your career with intention.
Source: Toronto Public Library — Young Adults

item.title: Ambunu Plant-based Hair Care — Wed Aug 5, 1:00 PM — Malvern
item.description: In celebration of Emancipation Month, join us to explore Ambunu, a traditional African botanical used for gentle hair cleansing and conditioning. This interactive workshop highlights the rich history of herbal hair care practices and the benefits of plant-based ingredients for scalp and hair wellness. Participants will learn about the science of natural hair care, including how different oils support scalp health and hydration. The session features a guided, hands-on activity where you’ll personalize a prepared Ambunu treatment using essential oils, while also learning about the full herbal preparation and formulation process. item.title: 🌳🍦 ST. CLAIR WEST VILLAGE EVENING WALK, WYCHWOOD PARK, ICE CREAM & MORE! 🍦🌳 — Wed Aug 5, 6:30 PM
item.description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years! 🌳🍦 ST. CLAIR WEST VILLAGE WALK, WYCHWOOD PARK, ICE CREAM & MORE! 🍦🌳
Hidden Streets, Storybook Homes & Some of Toronto’s Best Ice Cream Some parts of Toronto feel like you've accidentally wandered into a completely different city.
Join us for a relaxed social walk through St. Clair West and the hidden enclave of Wychwood Park — one of Toronto's most unique and exclusive residential communities.
Wychwood Park is private, residential, and unlike anywhere else in the city. The homes are all architecturally distinct — no cookie-cutter subdivisions here. Living in Wychwood Park involves a waiting list, board approval, and community guidelines designed to preserve the character of the neighbourhood.
It feels almost village-like... peaceful, artistic, and slightly secret. This is not a formal historical tour.
It's a social walk with beautiful surroundings, interesting neighbourhoods, and good conversation.

item.title: Diversifying Your Income: Arts Mentor in Residence Series with Elaine Chan-Dow — Thu Aug 6, 6:00 PM — Malvern
item.description: Creative careers often involve balancing multiple income streams and opportunities. In this workshop on diversifying your income, explore approaches to freelance work, commissions, grants, teaching and community-based opportunities. Participants will also learn strategies for professional outreach, cold-emailing and building a sustainable step-by-step plan tailored to their goals. This program will be followed by a Q&A. This workshop is presented by transdisciplinary artist, educator and researcher Elaine Chan-Dow, whose art and research practice explores culture, environmental sustainability and contemporary creative practice. Learn more about the Arts Mentor in Residence program, including workshops and one-on-one consultations. item.title: Bibimbap Rice Bowl with Chef Sang — Thu Aug 6, 6:30 PM — Taylor Memorial
item.description:
Award-winning writer, chef, and TV personality, Sang Kim, teaches participants how to create a classic Korean rice bowl. Participants will learn each component ingredient, how to properly use a knife to chop and slice, and create their own sauce. During this hands-on, one-hour workshop, Chef Sang will demonstrate how to make nutritious rice bowls, based on Asian traditions. Each participant will construct an entire rice bowl with a variety of seasoned vegetables, cooked egg, and spicy-sweet-vinegary sauce. Cooked ingredients will be prepared in advance. Participants have the option of not using the egg and keeping it strictly vegetarian. This program is for Young adults 18 to 24 (*contains egg, sesame oil, sesame seed)
Source: Toronto Public Library — Young Adults

item.title: Business Inc. Virtual Information Session — Fri Aug 7, 12:00 PM
item.description: Join our Fall 2026 Business Inc. Virtual Info Session to learn about this 8-week program supporting Toronto entrepreneurs to launch and grow. Do you have a small business or idea and want tailored feedback and support to take it to the next level? Join the Business Inc. Program to connect with experienced mentors and other entrepreneurs that will help you grow. During eight weekly sessions, entrepreneurs will learn business fundamentals, get clarity on the viability of their business ideas, get feedback and reviews from professional business advisors, discuss with and learn from their peers, and build a foundation for success. A general stream will run weekly at Deer Park branch on Thursday evenings from October 22 – December 10, from 6 - 9pm. A general stream will run weekly at North York Central Library on Tuesday evenings from October 20 – December 8, from 6 - 9pm. The Newcomer Entrepreneur stream will run weekly at Runnymede branch on Wednesday evenings from October 7 – November 25

item.title: What's the Worst That Can Happen?: Writing Dystopian Fiction With Rachel A. Rosen — Sat Aug 8, 2:30 PM — Lillian H. Smith
item.description: From classics like Margaret Atwood’s Handmaid’s Tale to modern takes such as Cherie Dimaline’s The Marrow Thieves or Catherine Hernandez’s Crosshairs , dystopian fiction is a mainstay of Canadian sci-fi and fantasy. Why do we seek out cautionary tales when the real world is already so bleak? And how can prospective writers of dystopian speculative fiction write believable, immersive worlds? Join us for a creative writing workshop hosted by Aurora Award nominee and author, Rachel A. Rosen! Through a series of activities and guided exercises, participants will develop a literary toolbox to deepen their world-building and generate ideas for their own writing. Hosted by the Merril Collection of Science Fiction, Speculation & Fantasy This event is intended for audiences age 18 and up. Please register for this event on our website as space is limited.
